functional.text: put(key, value), get(key), delete(key); keys ≤ 256 B, values ≤ 1 MB (avg ~1 KB).
Per-request consistency knobs: callers can ask for quorum reads/writes or fastest-possible.
Add or remove servers without downtime.

non_functional.text: Highly available: writes are never refused because of node failures or a network partition (AP by default).
Eventually consistent by default; concurrent writes are surfaced as conflicts, not silently lost; tunable per request.
p99 latency < 10 ms for get and put at 1M reads/s and 200k writes/s.
Durable: data survives the loss of any single node or one availability zone.

assumptions.text: 20B keys × ~1.2 KB per entry incl. key and metadata; 4 TB disk per server, kept ≤ 50% full.
One region, 3 AZs; some node fails every week.

out_of_scope.text: Range scans, secondary indexes, multi-key transactions, cross-region replication.

api.request: value, context (opaque version vector from the last get), w?
api.notes: Context lets the store tell an overwrite from a concurrent write.
Several values = concurrent siblings; the client merges and writes back with the context.
Writes a tombstone (garbage-collected after the repair window).

data.name: record
data.fields: key, value, version vector [(node_id, counter)…], tombstone flag, write timestamp, checksum
data.why: Per-node LSM tree (WAL + memtable + SSTables with bloom filters): fast writes, point reads in one or two disk seeks.

data.name: ring map
data.fields: virtual node token → physical node, per-node status (up/suspect/down), generation
data.why: Small; held in memory on every node and spread by gossip.

parts.title: Partitioning: which nodes own a key
parts.problem: Spread 72 TB and 2.6M replica ops/s over ~40 nodes so that adding a node (≈20 a year) moves little data and doesn't overload one peer.

options.name: hash(key) mod N
options.cons: changing N remaps almost every key: a full reshuffle on each growth step

options.name: range partitioning with a split manager
options.cons: hot ranges on sequential keys; needs a central split/merge manager, and scans are out of scope

options.name: consistent hashing with virtual nodes
options.pros: adding a node moves ~1/N of keys, taken from many peers in parallel; more vnodes for bigger machines
options.cons: a ring map every node must agree on; no range scans

parts.choice: Consistent hashing with ~256 virtual nodes per server
parts.why: F3 and 50% growth a year: a new node takes small slices from ~40 peers, so rebalancing moves ~1/N of 72 TB and the streaming load is spread, not concentrated on one neighbour. Scans are out of scope, so we lose nothing by hashing.

nodes.label: Request coordinator (any node: N=3, R=2, W=2)

parts.title: Replication and quorums
parts.problem: Keep every key alive through a node or AZ loss, never refuse a write, and still let callers ask for fresher reads.

options.name: single leader per partition (Raft/Paxos group)
options.cons: writes stall during leader election; a partition that isolates the leader refuses writes (breaks N1)

options.name: leaderless, N=3, strict quorum
options.pros: no failover; R + W > N gives overlapping reads
options.cons: a write fails when 2 of its 3 owners are unreachable

options.name: leaderless, N=3, sloppy quorum + hinted handoff
options.pros: a write always finds W healthy nodes, even mid-partition
options.cons: a read may briefly miss a write that sits as a hint on a stand-in node

parts.choice: Leaderless, N=3 (one replica per AZ), W=2, R=2 by default, with a sloppy quorum
parts.why: N1 forbids refusing writes and N4 needs a copy in each AZ. R + W > N (2 + 2 > 3) gives read-your-writes in the normal case; callers who need speed choose W=1/R=1, callers who need freshness choose R=3.

nodes.label: Request coordinator (any node: N=3, R=2, W=2)

parts.title: Conflict resolution for concurrent writes
parts.problem: With leaderless writes, two sides of a split can both accept a put to the same cart. A later read must neither lose one silently nor pick at random.

options.name: last-write-wins on wall-clock timestamps
options.cons: clock skew silently drops a write: a lost cart item

options.name: version vectors, siblings returned to the client
options.pros: detects true concurrency; nothing is lost; the app merges
options.cons: clients must merge; vectors grow (prune old entries)

options.name: CRDT values (sets, counters, maps)
options.cons: only for the data types you implement; heavier metadata

parts.choice: Version vectors with siblings returned to the client; LWW as an opt-in per table
parts.why: N2 and the cart team's request: detect concurrency instead of guessing. A put carries the context of the read it was based on, so the store can tell an overwrite (descendant) from a concurrent write (sibling). Teams that don't care opt into LWW.

nodes.label: Request coordinator (any node: N=3, R=2, W=2)

parts.title: Failure detection and repair
parts.problem: Some node is down every week. The cluster must notice it, keep accepting its writes, and bring it (or its replacement) back in sync.

options.name: central heartbeat monitor
options.pros: one simple view of the cluster
options.cons: a single point of failure; the monitor's own partition causes false alarms

options.name: gossip + phi-accrual failure detector, then hints, read repair and Merkle-tree anti-entropy
options.pros: decentralised; each tool covers one time scale of drift
options.cons: membership converges in seconds, not instantly; more moving parts

parts.choice: Gossip membership with a phi-accrual detector; hinted handoff, read repair and Merkle-tree anti-entropy
parts.why: Three time scales of drift: minutes (a neighbour keeps hints and replays them), per read (repair a stale replica the read just saw), and long term (compare Merkle trees per range and stream only the keys that differ). No central monitor to fail.

nodes.label: Request coordinator (any node: N=3, R=2, W=2)
Node D (AZ3) holds hints for C

parts.title: Storage engine on each node
parts.problem: Each node takes ~72k replica ops/s, mostly random-key writes, and must answer a point read in a few milliseconds without losing acknowledged writes on a crash.

options.name: B-tree (update in place)
options.cons: random writes rewrite pages: write amplification and SSD wear at our write rate

options.name: LSM tree: WAL + memtable + immutable SSTables + compaction
options.pros: writes are sequential appends; bloom filters keep reads to ~1 disk seek; tombstones fit naturally
options.cons: compaction I/O spikes; reads may check several SSTables

options.name: in-memory hash table + log
options.cons: 24 TB per replica set doesn't fit in RAM at a sane cost

parts.choice: LSM tree: commit log, memtable, SSTables with bloom filters, size-tiered/leveled compaction
parts.why: The workload is write-heavy and point-lookup only. Sequential appends keep p99 under 10 ms at ~72k ops/s per node, fsync batching on the WAL makes acked writes durable, and bloom filters skip SSTables that can't hold the key.

deep_dives.title: Deletes, tombstones and resurrection

options.name: remove the key physically on delete
options.cons: a replica that missed the delete later 'repairs' the old value back to life

options.name: write a tombstone, purge it after a grace period longer than the repair window
options.pros: deletes replicate like writes; no resurrection
options.cons: tombstones cost disk and slow reads until compaction purges them

deep_dives.choice: Tombstones with a 10-day grace period; anti-entropy must complete within it
deep_dives.why: A delete is just another versioned write, so hints, read repair and Merkle repair spread it. Purging only after every replica has certainly seen it (repair runs at least weekly) prevents deleted carts from reappearing.

deep_dives.title: Hot keys

options.name: do nothing: 3 replicas share the load
options.cons: one viral key pins three nodes at 100% and raises p99 for their other keys

options.name: client-side cache with a short TTL for read-hot keys
options.cons: stale reads for up to the TTL

options.name: salt write-hot keys into k sub-keys and merge on read
options.cons: reads fan out k ways; the app must know

deep_dives.choice: Client-side TTL cache for read-hot keys; salting only for known write-hot counters
deep_dives.why: Per-node budgets assume uniform load (~72k ops/s each); a hot key breaks that assumption on 3 nodes. Most hotness is reads, which a 1 s cache removes cheaply.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Hot keys (one partition's three replicas take the load: client-side caching or key salting), compaction I/O spikes on LSM nodes (throttle), rebalancing traffic when adding nodes (rate-limited streaming).
wrapup.failures: Single node down: sloppy quorum + hinted handoff, callers see nothing. AZ cut off: the other two AZs still form W=2/R=2. Silent disk corruption: block checksums + Merkle repair from peers. Permanent node loss: its vnodes are re-replicated from surviving copies.
wrapup.monitoring: p99 get/put latency per node, quorum failures, hint backlog size, read-repair rate, sibling count per key, disk fill, compaction backlog, gossip convergence time.
wrapup.scale: Add servers: they claim vnodes from many peers and stream in parallel, throttled; ring updates gossip out; no downtime. Growth of 50%/year ≈ 20 new nodes a year.
wrapup.future: Cross-region async replication, range scans via an order-preserving partitioner for some tables, tiered storage for cold keys.
